chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who deliberately left the Sa'y (circumambulation), he said: 'He must perform Hajj next year.' Regarding a man who left some of the Ramal (fast walking) in his Sa'y between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, he said: 'There is nothing upon him.' And whoever began with Al-Marwah before As-Safa, he must repeat it. It was narrated.

key_terms.اَلرَّمَل: Fast walking with short steps, a recommended act during the first three circuits of Sa'y
key_terms.اَلسَّعْي: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.اَلصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which Sa'y is performed
key_terms.اَلْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwah, the second hill in the Sa'y ritual

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to perform Ramal or starts Sa'y in the wrong order?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the hierarchy of obligations in Hajj rituals, distinguishing between essential pillars (*arkan*) and recommended acts (*sunan*). The ruling that deliberate omission of Sa'y necessitates repeating the entire Hajj underscores its status as a fundamental pillar, whereas the leniency for missing Ramal or starting with Marwah highlights the flexibility in the sequence of these ritual movements.
